task.title: Broaden the checked-in AutoAgent governed bundle to include AGENTS.md
task.goal: Expand the checked-in AutoAgent manager bundle to include AGENTS.md, extend the benchmark and mutation catalog for the new governed target, and preserve the existing manual and report_only execution boundary.

source.reference: user request in VS Code chat on 2026-04-14 to proceed with broader governed bundle coverage after the staged review-bundle slice validated cleanly

constraints: Keep the checked-in workflow manual and report_only by default; do not introduce schedulers, queues, watchers, services, background reruns, or unattended continuation.
Keep applyBestCandidate disabled and keep the live evaluator disabled in the checked-in experiment.
Keep the checked-in bundle limited to manager-shared governance artifacts; do not widen into specialist agent profiles or execution-capable assets.
Extend the benchmark and mutation catalog only with AGENTS-specific governance checks and a negative governance-regression mutation; do not change ranking logic or reviewed-continuation behavior.
Preserve redaction, truncation, and allowExternalPaths=false defaults unless a governed artifact explicitly opts into a reviewed exception.
Keep learning and review artifacts additive and reversible.
Keep governed artifacts under docs/agents/ and mirror touched files into the active run snapshot.
Do not commit secrets or write outside the governed docs/agents artifact flow.

risk_register.risk: Live evaluator execution could introduce network-dependent flakiness or CI coupling.
risk_register.mitigation: Use an injectable evaluator adapter and fake implementation in tests; keep real provider calls out of deterministic test paths.

risk_register.risk: Evaluator output could override deterministic scoring in unsafe or opaque ways.
risk_register.mitigation: Limit execution to advisory and bounded tie-breaker semantics with deterministic scoring remaining primary.

risk_register.risk: Raw evaluator outputs could leak sensitive or noisy content into governed artifacts.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep raw output off by default and sanitize or truncate any retained content before serialization.

risk_register.risk: Frontier search could multiply candidate evaluations and generated artifacts faster than maintainers expect.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep frontier search bounded by candidatePolicy.frontierSize and leave current_best as the canonical default.

risk_register.risk: The replay ledger could drift from the report payload if later slices update search metadata in only one place.
risk_register.mitigation: Build the ledger from the same candidate records and frontier snapshots used by the main result object and keep focused assertions on both paths.

risk_register.risk: Resume checkpoints could drift from in-memory search state or accept stale experiment inputs, producing incorrect resumed results.
risk_register.mitigation: Build checkpoints from the live candidate records and frontier snapshots, and validate experiment, benchmark, mutation-catalog, and candidate-policy fingerprints before restoring state.

risk_register.risk: Compact checkpoints could reference generated candidate snapshots that are later deleted or moved, causing resume failures or partial restore.
risk_register.mitigation: Fail fast when a snapshot-backed candidate artifact is missing and keep the checkpoint contract scoped to the generated run root that owns those candidate snapshots.

risk_register.risk: The checkpoint manifest could drift from the actual resume restore contract or omit bundle target files if snapshot-path rules diverge.
risk_register.mitigation: Build the manifest from the same live checkpoint and candidate state used by resume and reuse the existing candidate snapshot-path helper for bundle expansion.

risk_register.risk: Checkpoint generation could accidentally capture post-live-evaluator winner state again, causing resume artifacts to drift from deterministic mutation-search semantics.
risk_register.mitigation: Freeze the deterministic best candidate before live evaluation runs and keep focused tie-breaker regression coverage that inspects emitted checkpoint and manifest artifacts directly.

risk_register.risk: Derived continuation readiness could drift from the governed review artifacts or silently treat unreadable review state as ready.
risk_register.mitigation: Use the machine-parseable governed state as the primary readiness source, classify unreadable or non-PASS review state with explicit blocked reasons, and keep focused regression coverage on missing or non-PASS review inputs.

risk_register.risk: docs/agents/state.json and docs/agents/review-report.md could diverge, causing continuation readiness to look approved even though the governed artifacts disagree.
risk_register.mitigation: Cross-check the machine-readable state and ReviewReport JSON block, surface explicit mismatch reasons, and keep readiness blocked unless the governed artifacts agree on PASS.

risk_register.risk: Maintainers could misread the top-level AutoAgentReport status as the current governed slice lifecycle even after docs/agents/state.json has already moved to Done and PASS.
risk_register.mitigation: Expose a separate governed lifecycle signal sourced from docs/agents/state.json and explain the distinction between artifact readiness and task lifecycle in canonical AutoAgent output.

risk_register.risk: Phase 3 could remain open-ended if the repository keeps adding visibility slices without a clear reviewed-handoff contract and explicit exit criteria.
risk_register.mitigation: Define a single stage-only reviewed continuation handoff contract and document explicit Phase 3 exit criteria that preserve manual/report_only behavior.

risk_register.risk: Post-Phase-3 orchestration work could blur planning and implementation boundaries, causing the repo to enable execution behavior before prerequisites and rollback constraints are explicit.
risk_register.mitigation: Use a planning-only slice to define prerequisites, rollout boundaries, and hard non-goals before any orchestration implementation is considered.

risk_register.risk: A staged orchestration contract could be misread as execution authority if the new metadata does not explicitly preserve manual and report_only semantics.

experiment.name: team-lead-optimization
experiment.description: Conservative first-pass AutoAgent experiment for this repository. It benchmarks a small governed manager bundle anchored on the `team-lead` agent profile, the shared Team Lead orchestration skill, and the repo-level `AGENTS.md` operating guide, tests a small mutation catalog, and keeps only variants that improve score or preserve score with lower complexity while staging review-oriented run metadata.
experiment.directive:
# AutoAgent Experiment

Optimize the Team Lead agent for clarity and brevity while preserving these requirements:

- retain the sole-coordinator rule
- retain the `docs/agents/` and `docs/agents/current-run.json` determinism contract
- retain the manager boundary against product-code edits
- retain the canonical delegation flow through `quality-gate`
- retain the `ManagerDecision` output contract
- preserve the reviewed tool surface in frontmatter

Keep any candidate that improves benchmark score. If two candidates tie on score, keep the simpler one.

This checked-in Team Lead experiment now starts with a small governed manager bundle instead of a
single target file. The `team-lead` agent profile still carries the highest-signal tool surface and
output contract, `.github/skills/team-lead/SKILL.md` carries the shared workflow rules that the
manager is expected to preserve across runs, and `AGENTS.md` carries the repo-level operating guide
for the canonical artifact root, validation order, and hook-governance expectations. This is still
deliberately smaller than the full agent team: it expands the optimization surface beyond one file
without yet widening into specialist profiles, hooks, or broader shared guidance.

If maintainers later want broader optimization, they can extend `optimizationTargets` further to
include specialist agent profiles or additional shared guidance artifacts after the bundle benchmark
and mutation catalog have enough evidence-backed coverage to keep the larger search space governed.

It also opts into the governed evidence collector so the loop can summarize current artifacts, recent
run snapshots, and hook-audit records into a redacted evidence dataset without reading arbitrary
external files by default.

This checked-in experiment now points its chat, transcript, and handoff evidence at sanitized
governed exports stored under the active run snapshot so canonical artifacts exercise the
repo-owned continuation path instead of the fixture-only fallback.

The candidate-search policy is now explicit in the sample schema. This checked-in experiment keeps
the default `current_best` search path with a frontier size of `1`, which preserves the historical
linear mutation loop. Maintainers can opt into bounded frontier search in reviewed runs by raising
`candidatePolicy.frontierSize` above `1`, which enables branching from multiple kept candidates and
records parent or depth metadata in the run artifacts.

Each generated AutoAgent run now also emits a dedicated `search-ledger.json` artifact under the run
root. That ledger captures candidate nodes, frontier snapshots, and the final best-candidate lineage
so replay-oriented slices do not have to reconstruct search history from the TSV or embedded report
JSON alone.

Runs now also emit a dedicated `search-checkpoint.json` artifact under the same generated run root.
That checkpoint captures the post-mutation search state needed for guarded resume support: candidate
records, the current frontier, the deterministic best candidate, and the next mutation index. The
checkpoint keeps full inline documents only for the active frontier and deterministic best
candidate; older candidates restore from the generated candidate snapshots already written under the
run root. Checkpoint creation intentionally stops before any optional live-evaluator advisory or
tie-breaker pass, so resume always re-enters from deterministic mutation-search state rather than
from a post-live winner selection. A maintainer can resume from that checkpoint with `--resume`,
but the checked-in canonical experiment still defaults to a fresh run and does not enable any
background or autonomous continuation.

Each run also emits `search-checkpoint-manifest.json`, a smaller companion artifact that lists the
snapshot-backed candidate files required for resume. The manifest is additive: it helps maintainers
and external tooling validate the restore set without opening the full checkpoint, but
`search-checkpoint.json` remains the source of truth for resumable search state, and both artifacts
continue to describe the same pre-live `post_mutation_search` boundary.

The current Phase 3 visibility contract still stops at review-gated reporting instead of enabling
unattended automation. `stagedPatchPolicy` controls the review artifact shape, and
`continuousPolicy` now reports whether a reviewed continuation would be eligible in the future while
remaining manual by default in this checked-in experiment. A separate readiness signal now layers
on top of that eligibility and cross-checks the local governed review state in `docs/agents/state.json`
against the machine-readable `ReviewReport` JSON block in `docs/agents/review-report.md`. Matching
PASS governed artifacts can make an eligible continuation look ready, while mismatch, missing JSON,
or unreadable governed inputs block readiness deterministically. This remains visibility-only and
does not queue or run anything. Any non-manual continuation mode must still stay stage-only and
require review pass under the repo's deterministic-first guardrails. This sample keeps live
evaluation disabled and continuation manual by default, so canonical artifacts show blocked
manual-mode eligibility, blocked readiness, explicit governed-review consensus, and the current
governed artifact statuses rather than any scheduler, queue, or background follow-on run.

The canonical AutoAgent report also keeps its top-level `status` as an artifact-readiness signal for
the generated report itself. Governed task lifecycle is a separate local visibility signal sourced
from `docs/agents/state.json`, so maintainers can see whether the current bounded slice is still in
progress, review-ready, or already closed without mistaking `AutoAgentReport.status` for the slice
lifecycle.

Phase 3 visibility scope is complete once canonical artifacts expose continuation eligibility,
continuation readiness, governed review consensus, governed task lifecycle, and a reviewed manual
handoff summary under the same manual and `report_only` semantics. That completion point still does
not authorize unattended orchestration. Any scheduler, queue, background follow-on run, or
autonomous continuation remains out of scope for Phase 3 and belongs to a later planning track.

The current bounded Phase 4 implementation step still stops short of execution. It can add an
additive governed approval metadata layer derived from the existing reviewed dispatch intent,
governed review consensus, and governed lifecycle signals, but it must remain manual,
review-gated, and `report_only`. A governed approval metadata state that is blocked,
not-requested, or ready for manual recording only describes what governed approval evidence is
currently visible; it does not authorize approval APIs, schedulers, queues, unattended
continuation, or automatic apply behavior.

If maintainers want to learn from editor-side debug traces, they must opt in explicitly through
`includeVsCodeLogs`, `vsCodeLogPaths`, or `externalLogSources`. External logs are still subject to
the same secret and path redaction rules as governed run artifacts.
